text:
julia: Hey team  got a surprise balance bill for an MRI I had last month at a local imaging center. Carrier paid some amount but I just got a $650 balance notice from the facility. The provider listed a different NPI on the claim than the radiologist who read it. What are our options to get this corrected?

owen (Benefits): Sorry that happened  that smells like a billing/rendering vs. facility NPI mismatch. First steps: upload the itemized bill + carrier EOB into our benefits portal or email benefits@redwood.com. We need the provider bill, EOB, and the date of service. We can open a claims dispute and ask the provider to rebill with the correct rendering provider NPI so the carrier can re-adjudicate.

julia: I have the paper bill and an eob pdf. The notice references "facility fee" and the clinic is a freestanding center but billed as hospital outpatient.

mike (Billing): Two paths here: 1) Ask the provider billing office to correct and resubmit the claim with the correct taxonomy/NPI/claim type (clinic vs hospital). Usually they can rebill within 60 days. 2) If provider refuses, we can file an appeal with the carrier attaching proof that the radiologist/NPI was in-network and that the service should be adjudicated under the in-network benefit. Get the radiology report and the rendering physician NPI if available.

claims-bot: Automated resources -> Sample appeal letter: https://intranet.redwood.com/claims/sample-appeal.pdf. State DOI surprise-billing guidance: https://state-doi.example/surprise-billing. Typical carrier turnaround for rebill or appeal: 30-45 days. If it's a surprise out-of-network balance and your state has an independent dispute resolution (IDR) or surprise billing law, we can initiate that process after carrier denial.

owen (Benefits): Add these details when you submit: itemized invoice, EOB, radiology report (PDF), provider billing contact, and any email/text showing appointment type (outpatient imaging). Include a short note asking provider to rebill as outpatient clinic with rendering NPI X if you have it. We will also contact the carrier on your behalf and flag it as a potential provider billing error.

julia: If provider rebills and carrier still denies, can Redwood escalate or cover while in dispute? I don't want the balance hitting my credit.

mike (Billing): We don't typically pay member balances unless the plan terms require it, but we can request member-protection steps: ask provider to hold collections while dispute is active and request an internal hold (we can provide a benefits confirmation letter to the provider showing the claim is under review). If collections start, save collection notices and let benefits know immediately  we can coordinate an appeals priority.

owen (Benefits): Also check whether this falls under state surprise billing protections (balance-billing banned for certain emergency/outpatient scenarios). If so, carrier or provider may be prohibited from collecting the balance. We will check the state rule and include that point in the appeal. Provide provider address so we can file to the proper state regulator if needed.

julia: Timeline? How long before this is resolved usually?

claims-bot: Typical: provider rebill and carrier reprocess: 2-6 weeks. Carrier internal appeal after denial: 30-45 days. State IDR or regulator escalation: can be 60-120 days depending on process. We will confirm intake within 2 business days after you send docs.

mike (Billing): Practical tip: ask the billing office for a corrected claim reference number and the person who will resubmit. Get that in writing (email) so we can chase. Also request a billing hold while dispute is open.

julia: Ok sending the EOB + bill + radiology pdf now. One more: should I ask the radiologist for a letter confirming they interpreted the study and listing their NPI?

owen (Benefits): Yes please  that letter is helpful. If you can get the rendering physician NPI and a note that they are in-network, attach it. We'll open the case and follow up with the provider and carrier. Thanks for flagging this.

claims-bot: Reminder: include screenshots of any patient portal messages and the billing notice. Put "SURPRISE BALANCE - Julia [lastname]" in the email subject for expedited handling.
